text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former Kenya Ports Authority boss Simeon Mkalla and 19 others are acquitted of charges of conspiracy to defraud the government of millions of shillings.
- The Public Accounts Committee summons business tycoon Ketan Somaia to explain his failure to deliver goods worth 202 million shillings to the government.
- Kenya Commercial Bank employees threaten to go on strike following reports that the bank is pressured to use its staff pension fund to buy land of questionable value.
- British High Commissioner to Kenya Simon Hemans says the Kenyan economy has undergone far reaching changes that have strengthened investor confidence.
- Opposition parliamentarian Paul Muite is barred from appearing before the University of Nairobi senate sub-committee probing the mysterious death of student leader Solomon Muruli.
- Cabinet Minister Nicholas Biwott scores a decisive victory in his legal battle over the ownership of Yaya Centre after the high court rejects stay proceedings pending appeal.
- A row is brewing between opposition figure Raila Odinga and party chairman Stephen Omondi over the leadership of the National Development Party.
- A former deputy governor of the Central Bank of Kenya, a suspect in the Goldenberg scandal, asks a constitutional court to protect him from embarrassment by the state at trial.
- Nairobi Mayor Dick Waweru is non-committal on allegations he was involved in a brawl with Kenyan exiles in Sweden. ($1=55 Kenyan shillings)
